lines.text:
Monday. 6:47 PM. Floor 34, Brickell.
Everyone else went home an hour ago. Out the glass, the bay is going pink.

lines.name: Natso SweetLou
lines.text: The Henderson deck. Redo it. All of it. On my desk by eight.

lines.name: You
lines.text: I sent it Friday. You signed off on it.

lines.name: Natso SweetLou
lines.text: And now I'm un-signing off on it. Problem?

lines.name: You
lines.text: No problem, Lou.

lines.name: Natso SweetLou
lines.text: Great. Oh, and I told the partners the new model was my idea. Team player, right?

You were fourteen the first time you saw it on TV.
A final table under hot lights. A man in dark glasses pushed every chip he had into the middle with nothing.

The room went silent. His opponent folded. He never showed.
He made it look like he could see the future.

lines.name: You
lines.text: Somewhere along the way I traded that for a lanyard.

2:13 AM. The deck is done.
You are not.

lines.name: Stranger
lines.text: You're doing the thing where you stare at the pie like it owes you money.

lines.name: You
lines.text: Long day.

lines.name: Stranger
lines.text: Long life, by the look of it. What do you do?

lines.name: You
lines.text: Spreadsheets. For a guy who takes credit for them.

lines.name: Stranger
lines.text: And what did you want to do?
He slides a red envelope across the counter.

lines.name: Stranger
lines.text: The Biscayne Championship. Saturday, noon. Two-fifty seat. It's paid.

lines.name: You
lines.text: Why would you give that to a stranger?

lines.name: Stranger
lines.text: Because I sat on that stool once. Somebody bought my pie too.

lines.name: Stranger
lines.text: Three things. Fold the junk. Pressure the scared ones. And near the money, think about what the money's worth, not the chips.

lines.name: You
lines.text: Who are you?

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: People call me Slick.

He drops cash for both checks and is gone before the bell over the door stops ringing.
Inside the envelope: a seat card, and one line in pen.
“People insist on calling it luck…”

Saturday. 11:40 AM. Biscayne Card Room, off the causeway.
Carpet from 1994. Coffee from this morning, maybe.

lines.name: Miles "The Snowplow" Gnomey
lines.text: Help you?

lines.name: You
lines.text: Somebody bought me a seat. The Biscayne Championship.

lines.name: Miles "The Snowplow" Gnomey
lines.text: Free seat? Lucky you. Table nine, seat four. Cards in the air at noon.
A hundred and eighteen players. Two hundred and fifty dollars a seat. You paid nothing, and your hands are shaking anyway.

lines.name: Natso SweetLou
lines.text: You look different. Did you finish the Henderson numbers?
(One line about how your Saturday went, written from your actual result.)

lines.name: Natso SweetLou
lines.text: Hello? I'm talking to you. Weekend's over, champ.
Nobody says you have to decide forever. Keep the paycheck and play around it, or walk now and bet on yourself. You can always quit later.
Seven more hours of spreadsheets. Your mind never leaves table nine.
Monday night. Your phone buzzes on the counter.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Saw your results from Saturday. Here's my offer.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Quit Lou. I'll put $2,000 in your account tomorrow. Not a loan. Don't make me regret it.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Or keep the job and play on the side. Your call, kid. It's the biggest one you'll make.
Decision time.

lines.name: You
lines.text: Lou. Redo it yourself.

Sent. No paycheck. No plan B.
You have never felt lighter.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Done. $2,000 is in your account. Not a loan. Don't make me regret it.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Rent is due on the first. Never play above your roll.

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: BRO. YOU QUIT YOUR JOB?? CALL ME

You keep the lanyard.
But tonight you open a new spreadsheet and name it BANKROLL.
$1,250 lands every Friday. Days for Natso SweetLou. Three sessions a week for the dream.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Smart. A paycheck buys you time to learn. Never play above your roll. Text me when you win something.

Biscayne Card Room, off the causeway. Carpet from 1994, palms out front, coffee from this morning, maybe.
Twenty tables, every one of them a classroom.

lines.name: Miles "The Snowplow" Gnomey
lines.text: Back again? Sign the list. One-two has a seat in ten. Nightly turbo kicks off at seven.

lines.name: Tommy "The Shark" Maio
lines.text: Hey, you're the kid from Saturday. Don't get cocky. This room eats dreamers for breakfast.

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Cute hoodie. Did it come with the free seat?

Mustich. Dad's money, a solver subscription, and a smile you want to wipe off.
He's been circling the Biscayne Classic all year.
Goal: win the Biscayne Classic, or build your bankroll to $10,000.
Lucky Seven. 1:40 AM. The pie is the same. You are a little poorer.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Tell me the hand that got you.

lines.name: You
lines.text: King-jack, early position. I raised. Got three-bet. Called. Flopped a jack. Lost everything to kings.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Then the hand didn't get you. The first decision did. From early, king-jack is a fold. Everything after was a story you told yourself.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Fold the junk. That's not advice, it's arithmetic. Your misses are on the Spacepad. Drill them until the fold is boring.

scenes.title: Bad beat: the cards do not care

lines.text: Lucky Seven Diner. Same stool, same pie. The feeling is not the same.

lines.name: You
lines.text: I did everything right. Every decision. And I'm out.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Then you had a good day. You just did not get paid for it.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Over one hand, the cards pay whoever they like. Over ten thousand, they pay whoever studied. Play for the ten thousand.

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Heard you got coolered. Brutal. Maybe this game just isn’t for everyone.

lines.name: You
lines.text: He's right about one thing. It isn't for everyone.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Good. Make sure it is for you. I keep count of the beats, by the way. The ones who make it all have a long list.
Bags and tags. Two hundred and twelve started this morning. Forty come back tomorrow, and you're one of them.

lines.name: Miles "The Snowplow" Gnomey
lines.text: Bag your chips, write your name on it. Day 2 is noon tomorrow. Don't be late.

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Look who survived. Don't get used to it.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Day 2. Go to sleep. Don't celebrate yet.
(The final table: who's waiting for you there.)

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Final table. Dad flew in for this. Don't embarrass yourself.

lines.name: You
lines.text: Let's play.
Final hand. Heads-up for the Biscayne Classic, and the whole card room is standing on chairs.
The last card hits the felt. The Biscayne Classic is yours.

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Enjoy it. Dad says the Classic is a rounding error.

lines.name: Tommy "The Shark" Maio
lines.text: Don't listen to him, kid. Thirty years I've been chasing that trophy. You earned it.

lines.name: Miles "The Snowplow" Gnomey
lines.text: Your name goes on the board by the cage. Permanent marker. Congratulations.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Saw the photo. Trophy, big grin, terrible lighting. Proud of you, kid.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Left something in your locker. Every champion needs a pair.

Inside: a pair of pixelated sunglasses and a note.
“Deal with it.”

If your first title is online: Slick texts instead. "Saw the screenshot. Your name at the top of the lobby. Proud of you, kid."
"Left something for you at the Lucky Seven. Every champion needs a pair."
(Final hand, from the real hand you played.)

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Write it down. Some people are born for this.

lines.name: You
lines.text: Good game. I'll see you again.
Final hand. Mustich shoves with his dad watching from the rail. Called. An ace on the river.
The room explodes. Mustich holds the trophy over his head like he bought it.

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Write it down, Florida. Some people are born for this.

lines.name: You
lines.text: (your reaction, from how you went out)

lines.name: Tommy "The Shark" Maio
lines.text: Next month, kid. That trophy isn't going anywhere.
Final hand. Tommy "The Shark" Maio turns over two kings and the whole rail stops breathing.
The river bricks. Thirty years at this card room, and the old man finally has his trophy.

lines.name: Tommy "The Shark" Maio
lines.text: Thirty years! You hear me? Thirty years!

lines.name: You
lines.text: (your reaction, from how you went out)

lines.name: Miles "The Snowplow" Gnomey
lines.text: His name goes on the board by the cage. Next month, it could be yours.
Final hand. All in, called, and the board runs clean.
The room comes to its feet. The Biscayne Classic has a new name on the board.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Somebody had to keep you humble, kid. (or the winner's own line)

lines.name: You
lines.text: (your reaction, from how you went out)

lines.name: Miles "The Snowplow" Gnomey
lines.text: The name goes on the board by the cage. Next month, it could be yours.

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: TEN THOUSAND?? FROM POKER?? AND YOU STILL WENT TO WORK TODAY???

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: im just saying. lou doesnt deserve you. the felt does
Before each level: the stage, the hands at this level, and Slick's tip with his face. At the final table, the rival's face and line.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Early levels: chips are cheap, mistakes aren't. Fold the junk and let them spew.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Bubble. The short stacks are terrified. The big stacks are licking their lips. Which one are you?

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Final table. Every pay jump is real money. Every chip is a decision.
Online: CF Tilt · Level 7 · blinds 400/800 · next level 5:00. Slick's tip arrives as a text.
ALL IN, big, in neon lime. "Final table · all in vs Mustich" when it's someone from the story.
Your hand and theirs. Their cards flip with a sting, and the bar shows the odds: 62% to win.
The flop. The turn. "The river...", a long breath, then the river.
"You hold!" or "Mustich holds." Pocket kings beats ace-queen. Stack 38 → 81 bb.
If they fold to your shove: "Mustich thinks it over. Then the cards go in the muck. They fold. The pot is yours."
Online: the same screen, against a screen name, with no story faces.
A speech bubble from a seat for a few seconds after a big moment. Online, it's a chat message instead.

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Enjoy it. Variance is a loan. (you win a big pot)

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Out already? Dad's going to love this. (he busts you)

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Maybe stick to the spreadsheets.

lines.name: Tommy "The Shark" Maio
lines.text: Kid. Don't let it go to your head. Let it go to your bankroll. (you double up)

lines.name: Tommy "The Shark" Maio
lines.text: That wasn't poker. That was weather. (a cooler)
Online: chat lines from screen names instead: nh · sick · lol ok · ship it · gl. Mustich and Tommy only talk live.
THE BUBBLE. 33 left · 32 paid.

lines.name: Miles "The Snowplow" Gnomey
lines.text: We are hand for hand! Dealers, stand up when your hand is done. Nobody leaves the table.

lines.name: Tommy "The Shark" Maio
lines.text: Thirty years, kid, and the bubble still makes my hands sweat.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Near the money, think about what the money's worth. Not the chips.
Online: a CF Tilt banner, HAND-FOR-HAND, and the chat: fold fold fold · pls no bubble. Slick's text is the same.
IN THE MONEY.

lines.name: Miles "The Snowplow" Gnomey
lines.text: That's the bubble! Everybody left is in the money.

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: ARE YOU IN THE MONEY?? SCREENSHOT IT
Online: a banner, You're in the money, and the chat: gg bubble boy. David's text is the same.
HEADS-UP. Both faces, both stacks: You 61 bb · Mustich 47 bb.

lines.name: Miles "The Snowplow" Gnomey
lines.text: Ladies and gentlemen, we are heads-up for the Biscayne Classic!

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Final table. Dad flew in for this. Don't embarrass yourself.
Online: a banner, HEADS-UP vs ripriver_88, with the stacks. No announcer, no film.
Cooler. Nothing you could do.
Kings into aces. All the chips go in, and you never had a chance.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: You played it right. That's all you control. People insist on calling it luck.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Bad beats are the tax on getting your money in good. Pay it and keep playing.
One of: The last card falls and the room comes apart. [Event]. Yours.  ·  They push the whole thing across the felt. Every chip.  ·  Phones up. Dealer standing. Floor staff grinning.

lines.name: You
lines.text: One of: YES. YES. YES.  ·  I never doubted it. Not once. (Twice.)  ·  Text Slick. Text David. Text everyone.

lines.name: Tommy "The Shark" Maio
lines.text: Kid. Don't let it go to your head. Let it go to your bankroll. (a witness at the venue; changes with who's there) (live)

Online: one of: The final table window flashes gold. First of 1,104.  ·  Three in the morning, alone in the apartment, and you just beat a thousand people.  ·  The chat fills with gg and one ship it. The laptop fan is the only applause.

One of: Not the trophy, but a walk to the cage. [$] from [event].  ·  The cashier counts it twice. You count it four times on the way home.  ·  Out before the end, but with money. And a plan for the next one.

lines.name: You
lines.text: One of: Good. Next time, further.  ·  Bankroll first. Glory later.  ·  That's rent. That's the roll. That's enough.

lines.name: Tommy "The Shark" Maio
lines.text: A cash is a cash. The trophy's next. (a witness at the venue; changes with who's there)
Online: one of: A cash lands in your CF Tilt balance. You refresh it twice to be sure.  ·  Out before the end, but paid.  ·  Min-cash. You close the laptop gently, like it might change its mind.
One of: Chair pushed back. Chips gone. The lights feel brighter.  ·  The long walk past tables that are still playing.  ·  No cash. No excuses. The felt doesn't care.

lines.name: You
lines.text: One of: Review the hands. Every one.  ·  Variance. Or me. Tomorrow I'll know which.  ·  Sleep. Study. Back tomorrow.

lines.name: Tommy "The Shark" Maio
lines.text: Happens to everybody. Back tomorrow. (a witness at the venue; changes with who's there)
Online: one of: You finished 214th. The table window closes by itself.  ·  Busted. The tab is gone before you can argue with it.  ·  The lobby keeps scrolling. Nobody noticed you leave.
One of: Set over set. Kings into aces. Whatever you call it, it hurt.  ·  All in good. Called by worse. The river did the rest.  ·  You did everything right and the deck said no.

lines.name: You
lines.text: One of: ...Brutal.  ·  Right play. Wrong deck.  ·  Don't tilt. Don't tilt. Don't tilt.

lines.name: Tommy "The Shark" Maio
lines.text: Brutal. Thirty years and that one still stings. (a witness at the venue; changes with who's there)
Online: one of: Aces into kings, in a window the size of a postcard. It still hurts full size.  ·  The hand history says you did everything right. The balance says otherwise.

5:10 AM. The causeway is empty and the bay is the colour of a nickel.
Tommy "The Shark" Maio is driving a 1998 Lincoln like it owes him money.

lines.name: Tommy "The Shark" Maio
lines.text: Thirty years at Biscayne. You know how many times I drove north for a game?

lines.name: You
lines.text: Once?

lines.name: Tommy "The Shark" Maio
lines.text: Never. Not once. Rings are for guys who think they're going somewhere.

lines.name: You
lines.text: So why are you driving?

lines.name: Tommy "The Shark" Maio
lines.text: Because you asked. And because the coffee at Silver Strike is free and mine is terrible.
He doesn't say the other thing. He doesn't have to. A man doesn't iron his lucky shirt for free coffee.
Silver Strike Casino. Forty tables under a ceiling painted like a sunset, and every one of them is playing for a ring.
A man at the rail wears four on one hand. He keeps flexing it so you'll ask.

lines.name: Miles "The Snowplow" Gnomey
lines.text: Look who it is. They've got me running the floor up here on weekends now. Table twelve, seat six. Seat open!

lines.name: Chris Schillings
lines.text: You're the kid who quit the cubicle? I was an accountant. Spreadsheets and everything.

lines.name: You
lines.text: How did you know?

lines.name: Chris Schillings
lines.text: You hold your chips like they're receipts. Stop it. Play your game, and let them find out who you are.

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Look who followed me north. New patch, see? Somebody pays me to wear their logo now. Try not to bust on the bubble.
Goal: win two Circuit rings and build a $40,000 bankroll.

The casino bar at 1 AM. Keno on a television nobody watches.
An enormous man in a white hat is holding court with a plate of wings.

lines.name: Armadillo Fatts
lines.text: Sit down, partner. Everybody who sits gets a story, and nobody gets a refund.

lines.name: Armadillo Fatts
lines.text: Ten years back, give or take. World Championship of Cards, last two players. Kid in dark glasses shoves the river with nothing. Seven-deuce. The whole country can see it on the little camera.

lines.name: Armadillo Fatts
lines.text: Other fella has the winner. Thinks four minutes. Folds. Wears a mask to this day, so nobody can read him twice.

lines.name: You
lines.text: I watched that. I was fourteen.

lines.name: Armadillo Fatts
lines.text: Everybody watched it. Then the kid goes on TV and says one thing. "People insist on calling it luck." Cockiest sentence I ever heard.
The line in your envelope. Word for word. In pen.

lines.name: You
lines.text: What happened to him?

lines.name: Armadillo Fatts
lines.text:
Same thing that happens to all of us. He went home.
Order the wings. They're better than the story.
The $400 Turbo Ring, final table. Mouthy Michael has been talking for six straight hours and has no plans to stop.

lines.name: Mouthy Michael
lines.text: You're thinking. Don't think. Thinking is how they get you. You call this? You're not calling this. You're NOT calling this.

Every word is built to put a voice in your head that isn't yours.
Then the break. Fifteen minutes. One message on your phone.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Is he talking?

lines.name: You
lines.text: He hasn't stopped since noon.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Then he's scared. Comfortable people don't need noise. Play the cards, not the soundtrack.

lines.name: Mouthy Michael
lines.text: ...You called. Of course you called. Nice hand. NICE HAND. I'm fine. I'm totally fine.
The Circuit floor at midnight. Chips being racked all around you. None of them are yours.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: You check too much.

lines.name: You
lines.text: I didn't have anything.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Neither did they. On a dry board the raiser bets small and often, and everybody without a pair goes away. You gave them a free card and a free look at you.

lines.name: You
lines.text: It felt like lying.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: It's not lying. It's telling them a story they already believe. Pressure the scared ones. Small bets, lots of them. It's in your misses. Go run them.
The tournament director slides a heavy ring across the felt. It's a size too big. You put it on anyway.

lines.name: Chris Schillings
lines.text: First ring. I still remember mine. Don't put it in a drawer. Wear it every day you play. Let it be heavy.

lines.name: Tommy "The Shark" Maio
lines.text: Thirty years. First time I ever drove north, and the kid takes a ring. I'm telling everyone it was my coffee.

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: A RING??? LIKE A CHAMPIONSHIP RING?? LIKE THE NBA???

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: PUTTING IT IN THE GROUP CHAT. RENAMING THE GROUP CHAT

lines.name: Natso SweetLou
lines.text: Saw your ring on Instagram!! Crazy! Quick q — do you still have the login for the Henderson drive?

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: One ring. Now go get another one. Don't celebrate in a place that sells chips.
A private elevator. A room above the casino with one table, eight chairs, and a man holding an unlit cigarette like a conductor's baton.

lines.name: Sammy Smokes
lines.text: The ring kid. Sit, sit. Is small game tonight. Ten thousand minimum.

Ten thousand is a quarter of everything you have.
The chairs are leather. The chips are clay. The room smells like money that was never worried.

lines.name: Sammy Smokes
lines.text: Is a nice hand you have in you, I can tell. Is not my hand. But is nice.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Who's upstairs?

lines.name: You
lines.text: Sammy Smokes. 10K minimum.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: The game you're not rolled for is always the best game in the building. That's how it gets you.
Three hours. You play the best poker of your life and you lose six thousand dollars of it.

lines.name: Sammy Smokes
lines.text: You play good. The money doesn't know. Money never knows. This is why we keep it far from the heart.

lines.name: You
lines.text: Is that your lesson?

lines.name: Sammy Smokes
lines.text: My lesson? Is that I can afford this room. Go downstairs, ring kid. Downstairs is where you get rich.
The Circuit's charity event. Celebrities, local news, a giant check. And at table one, in the same hat for fifty years, Colt the Cowboy.

lines.name: Colt the Cowboy
lines.text: Son, I was playing this game before your daddy could shuffle. Sit. Let's see if they taught you anything.
He raises with ten-deuce, shows it, and wins the pot. The table laughs. He doesn't.

lines.name: Colt the Cowboy
lines.text: Everybody laughs at the ten-deuce. That's why it works. You know who I taught that to? Skinny kid. Dark glasses. Calle Ocho.

lines.name: You
lines.text: The Lucky Seven?

lines.name: Colt the Cowboy
lines.text: Bought him a slice of pie there once. Night he came home. A year after the big one, and every dollar of it gone. Soaked through, and he wouldn't take off those glasses.

lines.name: Colt the Cowboy
lines.text: He still buying people's pie?
Lucky Seven Diner. 2:13 AM. Two rings on the counter next to the pie.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Two rings and forty thousand dollars, none of it borrowed. That's a bankroll. You're not a tourist any more.

lines.name: You
lines.text: I met Colt the Cowboy.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Everyone meets Colt eventually. He's like weather.

lines.name: You
lines.text: He said he bought a broke kid in dark glasses a slice of pie here. The night he came home.
Slick turns his coffee cup a quarter turn. Then another. He doesn't look up.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Eat your pie. The Summer starts in June, and Vegas doesn't care who you met.
Goal complete. Chapter 3: The Summer.
Every June, the WCoC Summer Series takes over Las Vegas. 112 degrees outside and 68 inside, with ten thousand people chasing the same gold.

lines.name: Miles "The Snowplow" Gnomey
lines.text: They hired me for the summer! Floor supervisor, rooms A through D. Six weeks, no sunlight. Seat open!

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Every kid who ever loved this game dreams about a bracelet. This is the room where they hand them out. Don't look at the ceiling.
You look at the ceiling. Everyone does. Banners of every champion, back to the year your father was born.
At the feature table sits a man in a black mask. Fourteen bracelets, more than anyone alive. Nobody has seen him smile. Nobody has seen most of his face.

lines.name: Bio "The Ghost"
lines.text: Kid. Stop looking at me and look at your cards.

lines.name: Phil Hellraiser
lines.text: Another internet kid. I'll see you at the final table. Probably not, though. Statistically, not.
Goal: win a gold bracelet.
$3,000 Six-Max. On your left, GG Negroni has been narrating everyone's hand for an hour, out loud, and he's mostly right.

lines.name: GG Negroni
lines.text: I put you on ace-queen. Am I close? I'm close. Your shoulders went up a quarter inch when the queen came.

lines.name: You
lines.text: Maybe I have kings.

lines.name: GG Negroni
lines.text: If you had kings you'd be bored, and you're not bored. You're doing math. Kings don't do math.
He folds. You had ace-queen.

lines.name: GG Negroni
lines.text: See? Close. Hey, no hard feelings. Ninety percent of this game is listening. The other ten is pretending you weren't.
A steakhouse with no prices on the menu. A sponsor's table for twelve. Somebody ordered a bottle you've seen on TV.

lines.name: Gus Handsome
lines.text: Seven-four suited. That's how I got here. Nobody believes me. That's also how I got here.

lines.name: Antonio Escandalo
lines.text: Pick a card. Any card. No, don't show me. Show the table.
You pick the queen of hearts. He doesn't touch the deck. It's under your steak knife.

lines.name: Antonio Escandalo
lines.text: Poker is the same trick. Everyone watches the hand that moves. Nobody watches the hand that doesn't.

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Speaking of tricks. Event nine. First bracelet. Thought you'd want to see it up close.
He's wearing it. Of course he's wearing it.

lines.name: Gus Handsome
lines.text: Don't let him in your head. The bracelet's real, but the guy's a rental. Have the crab.
Two hundred and eleven players left. Two hundred get paid. You were two hundred and twelve.
The hallway outside the ballroom. Fluorescent lights. A bracelet poster with somebody else's face on it.

lines.name: Stu Hungar
lines.text: First bubble in the big room? Kid, I've seen this hallway from every angle. Lying down, mostly.

lines.name: You
lines.text: You're Stu Hungar.

lines.name: Stu Hungar
lines.text: Was. Then wasn't. Then was again. They call it a comeback. It's just showing up after everyone stopped expecting you.

lines.name: Stu Hungar
lines.text: Kid, I've seen this hand before. You haven't. Go learn why it hurts, then come back tomorrow.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: You called a shove with ace-ten on the bubble.

lines.name: You
lines.text: I was ahead of his range.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Ahead of his range in chips. Behind in money. Near the bubble, the chips you lose are worth more than the chips you win. That's the whole of ICM.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Think about what the money's worth, not the chips. The spot's on your Spacepad. Drill it till it stops hurting.

lines.name: You
lines.text: You could've just said "fold".

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Then you'd fold this one and call the next one. I'd rather you knew why.
$10,000 Heads-Up. Your opponent hasn't raised in forty minutes. He has a glass of water and all the time in the world.

lines.name: Chance Cage
lines.text: Take your time. I always do.
You bet. He calls. You bet. He calls. You bet everything.

He shows a full house he's been holding since the flop.
He hasn't raised in forty minutes because he hasn't needed to.

lines.name: Chance Cage
lines.text: The loudest thing at a poker table is a man who's waiting. You'll hear it next time.

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: BRO. SATURDAY. YOU'RE COMING. KATIE SAID YES AND YOU ARE THE FIRST PERSON I TOLD AFTER MY MOM
Saturday is the $5,000 Eight-Handed. Your best event of the summer, on paper.

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: (if you fly home) YOU CAME??? YOU ACTUALLY CAME??? KATIE HE CAME
(if you stay) its cool. go win. All lowercase. David has never typed lowercase in his life.
The mixed-game room. Eight games in rotation, and a kid in a backwards cap who has won three bracelets in five weeks.

lines.name: Nicky Parmesan
lines.text: Pick a game. Any game. I'll still be the favourite, but it'll be fun for you.

lines.name: You
lines.text: Hold'em.

lines.name: Nicky Parmesan
lines.text: Respect. Knowing your one game is a skill. Most people find out what it is the expensive way.
Heads-up for the $1,500 Opener bracelet. Across from you: Erik Seikick. Thirty years at the top of this game, and he hasn't said a word to you all night.

The last card. They fasten the bracelet on your wrist, and the room is clapping before you realise it's for you.
Gold. Real gold. Your name in the book forever.

lines.name: Erik Seikick
lines.text: You played well.
Three words. People have waited thirty years for three words from Erik Seikick.

lines.name: Phil Hellraiser
lines.text: Lucky. If I'd been at that final table, we'd be talking about my bracelet number eighteen.

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: IS THAT REAL GOLD?? THE WHOLE GROUP CHAT SAW IT. KATIE CRIED. I CRIED. I'M STILL MAD BUT I CRIED

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Fourteen-year-old you is screaming right now. Let him.
4 AM. The sportsbook is empty except for highlights of a game that ended hours ago.
Someone sits two stools down. The mask hangs off one ear, and the face under it is older than you expected.

lines.name: Bio "The Ghost"
lines.text: Nice bracelet.

lines.name: You
lines.text: You've got fourteen.

lines.name: Bio "The Ghost"
lines.text: I've got fourteen. You've got one that matters more. The first one is the only one you don't win for anybody else.

lines.name: Bio "The Ghost"
lines.text: You wait like somebody taught you to. I only know one man who teaches that.
He stands. He leaves a tip on the bar for a bartender who isn't there.

lines.name: Bio "The Ghost"
lines.text: Tell Slick I said hello.
He's gone before you can ask how he knows the name.
Lucky Seven Diner. 2:13 AM. You didn't text first. He was already there.

lines.name: You
lines.text: Bio says hello.
For a long time, nothing. The pie case hums. A car goes by with its windows down, playing something sad in Spanish.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: World Championship of Cards. Last two players. I had seven-deuce and a river that missed everything, and I knew he had me beat. I could see it on him.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: So I shoved. I didn't look at the board. I looked at him. And I watched him start to doubt he was allowed to win.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Four minutes. Then the best player I ever sat with folded the best hand he ever held, and the whole world watched it on a little camera.

lines.name: You
lines.text: The man in the dark glasses was you. And the one who folded was Bio.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: They asked me how. I said "people insist on calling it luck". Cockiest thing I ever said. Then I spent a year proving I could do it every night, above my roll, until the game took back every dollar.

lines.name: You
lines.text: And Colt bought your pie.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text:
Colt bought my pie.
I write that line on the envelopes so somebody proves it right the long way. It wasn't luck. I read a person, and the person flinched. Everything I've taught you is so you never flinch, and so you never think one great read makes you bulletproof.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Now finish your pie. You've got cameras next week, and cameras love a flinch.
A soundstage in Hollywood, Florida. Three cameras, a hole-card reader, and forty thousand people watching you blink.

lines.name: Nick "Baby Goat" Twogloves
lines.text: Welcome back to the Let's Go! Tour feature table! Joining us tonight: the cubicle kid with a bracelet. The chat's calling it a fluke.

lines.name: You
lines.text: People insist on calling it luck.

lines.name: Nick "Baby Goat" Twogloves
lines.text: OH. We have a quote. Producers, T-shirt. Now.
Under the lights everything shows. The rail can see your cards. The table can see your face.

lines.name: Kristen Foxglove
lines.text: Cameras make people do stupid things. Don't be people.

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: youre on the STREAM. my mom is watching. MY MOM. SIT UP STRAIGHT
Goal: win two Tour titles (Let's Go! Tour or One Time! Cup) and build a $750,000 bankroll.
The river. Tom Duhhz pushes a stack worth more than your first year on Floor 34 into the middle, and smiles at the camera like it's an old friend.

lines.name: Tom Duhhz
lines.text: I have air. Do you want to find out?

lines.name: Nick "Baby Goat" Twogloves
lines.text: The hole-card cam says... folks, he is not lying. He has ABSOLUTELY nothing. The question is whether our cubicle kid believes him.

Somewhere a fourteen-year-old is watching a river jam on a little camera.
This time you know which seat you're in.

lines.name: Tom Duhhz
lines.text: Truth is the best bluff. Nobody believes it.
The stream is over. The chat has moved on. The hand hasn't.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: You bluffed the one guy who never folds.

lines.name: You
lines.text: The board was perfect for it.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Perfect for a bluff against a player who folds. He doesn't. A bluff is a bet against a person, not a board. Pick the person first.

lines.name: You
lines.text: Is that what you did to Bio?

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: I picked the person first. Then the card. Then the moment. In that order. Ranges, not hands. People, not boards. Drill the river spots.

The One Time! Cup VIP lounge. Free shrimp. A banner reading "Halvorsen & Pike: Proud Partner".
You know that logo. You used to wear it on a lanyard.

lines.name: Natso SweetLou
lines.text: Buddy!! There he is! I told the partners we go way back. Mentor-mentee kind of thing.

lines.name: You
lines.text: You made me redo the Henderson deck at seven PM on a Monday, Lou.

lines.name: Natso SweetLou
lines.text: And look at you now! Character building. Quick photo for LinkedIn? "Proud to have shaped this talent."
One Time! Cup, $25,000. Pat Finny hasn't moved in nine minutes. Not his hands. Not his eyes. Possibly not his heart.

lines.name: Pat Finny
lines.text: Your move.
You try it. Stillness. Breath through the nose. Hands flat. The camera finds nothing to love.

lines.name: Pat Finny
lines.text: Better. Next time, also stop blinking.

lines.name: Nick "Baby Goat" Twogloves
lines.text: Let's look at the Player of the Year race! Up top, as always, Shane Dawb. Then the Tour Machine, Alex Foxglove. Mark Holdz in third, because he played every event on Earth.

lines.name: Shane Dawb
lines.text: Another one for the cabinet. The cabinet's getting crowded. I might need a second cabinet.

lines.name: Alex Foxglove
lines.text: Leaderboard points are points. You want in on the race, you play the schedule. All of it.

lines.name: Mark Holdz
lines.text: Shove.

lines.name: Nick "Baby Goat" Twogloves
lines.text: That was the whole interview. Mark Holdz, ladies and gentlemen. And, new on the board in fourteenth, the cubicle kid.

lines.name: Nick "Baby Goat" Twogloves
lines.text: Champion! Fifty thousand people on the stream. How does it feel?

lines.name: Kristen Foxglove
lines.text: Nice result. Now everyone has a file on you. Welcome to the Tour.
Two Tour titles. Three quarters of a million dollars. A trophy shaped like a crown, which is a lot even for television.

lines.name: Nick "Baby Goat" Twogloves
lines.text: And somebody left this at the desk for you. Black envelope. Embossed. Very James Bond.
Inside: the Titan. Invitation only. Buy-ins from one hundred thousand dollars.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Those rooms don't have scared people in them. Bring the part of you that isn't scared either.
A private terminal. A plane with your name on the manifest. A buy-in that used to be a house.
Nobody in this room is scared. That's the problem with it.

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Funny. Dad stopped staking me last month. Said I needed to "find out what it costs". So I guess we're both self-made now.

lines.name: You
lines.text: Welcome to the club. The dues are terrible.

lines.name: Linus Loophole
lines.text: I reviewed your last final table. Your bubble frequencies are... acceptable. Your river frequency is off by four percent.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: In there nobody's scared. Everyone knows the maths. So the edge is in the spots they don't study. Find them.

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: a HOUSE. you bought in for a HOUSE. im not telling your mother
Goal: win two Titan titles and build a $5,000,000 bankroll.
The hotel's top-floor bar. Bryan Dartfrog drinks sparkling water and talks about seven-figure buy-ins the way other people talk about parking.

lines.name: Bryan Dartfrog
lines.text: The $250K is next week. You've got the skill. You don't have the roll. I'll buy half your action. Fair price.

lines.name: You
lines.text: And if I win?

lines.name: Bryan Dartfrog
lines.text: Then I win half. And you win the other half, plus you got to play the biggest game on the planet like it was a one-two.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Selling action isn't weakness. Playing above your roll is. Never confuse the two.
5:02 AM. The hotel gym. Someone has been on the treadmill since before you were awake.

lines.name: Jay Cocoon
lines.text: Five AM gym, six AM study, Titans by dinner. You up early, or up late?

lines.name: You
lines.text: Up late.

lines.name: Jay Cocoon
lines.text: That's the difference between us. Not talent. I've got talent too. Discipline beats talent. I've got both.

lines.name: Jay Cocoon
lines.text: Get on the bike. Ten minutes. Your decisions after hour eight will thank you.
A conference room turned war room. Two laptops, a whiteboard of hand ranges, and the two most precise players alive arguing about a three percent frequency.

lines.name: Fedor Holdum
lines.text: I studied this exact spot this morning. River, four-bet pot, ninety big blinds. You check more than you should.

lines.name: Linus Loophole
lines.text: He checks four percent more than he should. Precision, Fedor.

lines.name: You
lines.text: How do you two ever lose?

lines.name: Fedor Holdum
lines.text: We play each other.
Everyone in this building has the same tools. Some of them have the same thoughts.
A room where everybody knows the maths. You lost anyway.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: They all have the same solver. So where's the edge?

lines.name: You
lines.text: There isn't one.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: There's one in every spot they don't study. Odd stacks. Four-bet pots. Limped pots with antes. The book is thin there. Be the one who read it.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: And one more spot nobody studies: the person across from you at hour eleven. The book is thinnest there.
The $50,000 Omaha. Four cards each, and every hand a tangle of possibilities. Isaac Maskedman is untangling them faster than you can see them.

lines.name: Isaac Maskedman
lines.text: Interesting sizing. Incorrect, but interesting.

lines.name: You
lines.text: What would you have bet?

lines.name: Isaac Maskedman
lines.text: Two-thirds pot. But I'd have known why. You bet two-thirds of something you felt. Feel less. Count more.
The $250,000. You lose the biggest pot of your life to a two-outer on the river. The room goes quiet in the polite way rich rooms go quiet.

lines.name: Stephen Chives
lines.text: That's brutal. I'm sorry. Genuinely.
He means it. In a room full of people trying to take everything you have, someone means it.

lines.name: Stephen Chives
lines.text: Final table every week, they say about me. They don't mention the weeks I didn't. Good luck tomorrow. Genuinely.
A trident-shaped trophy, a wire transfer with too many zeros, and a room full of the best players alive nodding at you.

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Congrats. Honestly. Turns out you can't buy what you've got. Believe me, I asked.

lines.name: You
lines.text: Took you long enough to figure that out.

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Ha. Rematch at the Main?

lines.name: Nick "Baby Goat" Twogloves
lines.text: Big question from the chat: where's Bio "The Ghost"? Biggest buy-ins in the world, and the GOAT is missing.

lines.name: Kristen Foxglove
lines.text: Bio doesn't play the Titan. Never has.

lines.name: Nick "Baby Goat" Twogloves
lines.text: Why not?

lines.name: Kristen Foxglove
lines.text: He says money isn't the score. Bracelets are. And there's only one he still cares about every year.
Five million dollars. Two tridents. And you're back on a stool at the Lucky Seven, because some things don't change when your bank balance does.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: The Main Event. July. Eight thousand players.

lines.name: You
lines.text: He'll be there.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text:
He's always there.
So am I, this year. I bought a ticket. First time in ten years.

lines.name: You
lines.text: You're coming to Vegas?

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Somebody has to buy your pie.

Every July: eight thousand players, ten thousand dollars each.
One of them ends up on the cover of every poker magazine in the world.
Day 1. A ballroom the size of an airport. Two hundred tables, and somewhere in the noise, a seat with your name on it.

lines.name: Miles "The Snowplow" Gnomey
lines.text: Main Event floor! They gave me the Main! Table one-eighty-eight, seat two. Seat open!

lines.name: Michael Mightyrocky
lines.text: Defending champ. If you want it, you'll have to take it from me.

lines.name: Bio "The Ghost"
lines.text: Still here, kid. So am I.
Goal: win the Main Event.
Day 1, level four. The player in seat nine has won nine titles this year, and he has decided the entire table is his personal property.

lines.name: Jesse Lonestar
lines.text: GORILLA. MODE.
He raises eleven hands in a row. On the twelfth you re-raise. He thinks. He folds. He grins.

lines.name: Jesse Lonestar
lines.text: There it is! Somebody at this table has a pulse! Nine wins this year, and the ones I remember are the ones somebody fought me for.
Day 5. The service hallway behind the ballroom. Linen carts, a vending machine, and Mustich, sitting on the floor in a five-thousand-dollar jacket.

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Bio. Of course it was Bio. He didn't even look at my cards. He looked at me like I was... furniture.

lines.name: You
lines.text: He does that.

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Dad's watching on the stream. Probably already writing the email. "Find out what it costs."
You sit down on the floor next to him. You're not friends. You're not anything. You sit anyway.

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Go win it. If anyone's taking him down, I want it to be someone who knows what this hallway feels like.
Two tables left. The defending champion, three seats to your right, has been grinding since Day 1 without a single bad day.

lines.name: Michael Mightyrocky
lines.text: You know they call me The Grinder? It's not because I'm fancy. It's because I'm still here when the fancy people go home.
The biggest pot of the tournament so far. His crown against your stack.

lines.name: Michael Mightyrocky
lines.text: Good. Good hand. I mean it. Take it the whole way, or I'll be mad I didn't.
The night before the final table. A 24-hour diner off Flamingo Road. Different city. Same hour.
He's already on a stool. Dark glasses. Two slices of pie.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Ten years since I set foot in this city. The pie's worse.

lines.name: You
lines.text: If it comes down to him and me. If he shoves the river.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Then it won't be about the cards. He'll look at you the way I looked at him. He's waited ten years to put somebody in the seat he was in.

lines.name: You
lines.text: What did you see in him that night?

lines.name: Slick
lines.text:
Doubt. He didn't doubt his hand. He doubted he was allowed to win.
Don't give him that. Whatever you decide, decide it like you're allowed.
He pays for both slices. He doesn't leave. For the first time, he stays until you do.
The final table. A stage, a wall of lights, and a rail packed three deep.

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: SIT UP STRAIGHT!
Not a text. David, in person, with a sign that says "PEOPLE INSIST ON CALLING IT LUCK" in a handwriting you'd know anywhere.

lines.name: Tommy "The Shark" Maio
lines.text: Thirty-one years. Second time I ever left Biscayne for a game. Somebody had to come make sure you don't get cocky.
Meanwhile, at a sports bar in Brickell, a man in a Halvorsen & Pike quarter-zip tells the bartender he used to manage you.

lines.name: Nick "Baby Goat" Twogloves
lines.text: From the booth, live, worldwide: welcome to the final table of the WCoC Main Event.
Heads-up. Bio "The Ghost" and you. Every chip in the building is on one table.

lines.name: Nick "Baby Goat" Twogloves
lines.text: Folks, this is the spot. River. The Ghost moves all in. And if you're old enough... you've seen this movie before.
He's not looking at the board. He's looking at you, the way a man in dark glasses once looked at him.
On the rail, a man in dark glasses takes them off.
You don't flinch. Whatever you do next, you decide it like you're allowed.

Confetti. Cameras. A bracelet the size of a doorknob.
Somewhere, a fourteen-year-old with a fuzzy TV is losing his mind.

lines.name: Bio "The Ghost"
lines.text: Good game, kid.
He takes off the mask. For the first time anyone can remember, Bio "The Ghost" smiles.

Then he looks past you, to the rail, and nods at a man he hasn't spoken to in ten years.
Slick nods back.

lines.name: Bio "The Ghost"
lines.text: Now you'll find out the hard part. Everyone will be hunting you.

lines.name: Natso SweetLou
lines.text: Hey buddy! Long time! Saw you on TV. Listen, about that promotion...
You leave him on read.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: People insist on calling it luck.

lines.name: You
lines.text: Let them.
Second in the world. Somebody else's confetti.

lines.name: Bio "The Ghost"
lines.text: You didn't flinch. That's rarer than winning. Come back next July.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: One hand, kid. Over ten thousand, they pay whoever studied. You studied.

lines.name: Nick "Baby Goat" Twogloves
lines.text: The kid lets it go! And the Ghost... doesn't show. Of course he doesn't show.

lines.name: Bio "The Ghost"
lines.text: You thought about it. Good. Most people only think about it afterwards.
On the rail, Slick puts his glasses back on. The match isn't over. Neither are you.
Your picture hangs in the Hall of Legends now, next to people you used to watch on a fuzzy TV.
Stu. Colt. Chance. The Ghost. Twenty-seven legends on these walls, and a kid from Floor 34 who got told to redo the Henderson deck.

lines.name: Bio "The Ghost"
lines.text: Fourteen bracelets. That's the number. Come take it.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: There's nobody left to teach you. So teach somebody. I sat on that stool once too, remember.

lines.name: You
lines.text: I remember.
Goal: beat every legend and pass Bio "The Ghost"'s fourteen bracelets.

lines.name: Stu Hungar
lines.text: Kid, I've seen this hand before. Let's see if you have.

lines.name: Colt the Cowboy
lines.text: Bring your ten-deuce, son. I'll bring mine.

lines.name: Chance Cage
lines.text: Take your time. I'll be waiting.

lines.name: Armadillo Fatts
lines.text: I've got a new story. It's about you. Come hear the ending.

lines.name: Phil Hellraiser
lines.text: Bracelet eighteen is coming. You'll be a nice footnote.

lines.name: GG Negroni
lines.text: I already know your cards. Want to make it official?

lines.name: Tom Duhhz
lines.text: I have air. Want to find out?

lines.name: Pat Finny
lines.text: Your move.

lines.name: Michael Mightyrocky
lines.text: Rematch. I'm still here.
The Hall of Legends Invitational, final table. Seat five, in a jacket he paid for himself this time: Mustich.

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Saw your portrait in the lobby. Very moving. They got your bad side.

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Dad sold the company. No more stake, no more rail. Turns out I still want to beat you. Annoying, isn't it?

lines.name: You
lines.text: For you? Very.

lines.name: Mustich
lines.text: Fifteen is just a number, Florida. Somebody's going to take it off you. I'd like it to be someone you can't stand.
He grins. The same grin from the Biscayne card room, the first night. You'd miss it if it ever went away. You'll never tell him that.
A reception hall in Hialeah. Fairy lights, a DJ who plays one song too many, and David Pec in a tuxedo he's been talking about since March.

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: My best man is a world champion. I told everyone. Everyone. The caterers know.

lines.name: You
lines.text: I missed your engagement party for a five-thousand-dollar event.

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: And you cashed for eleven grand and sent us to Cancún. Bro. I forgave you in the airport.
You stand up to give the speech. You had cards. You put them away.

lines.name: You
lines.text: The first person who ever believed I could do this wasn't a pro. He texted in all caps, and he was right.
The Hall's annual dedication. Twenty-seven frames, and one blank space on the wall that's been there for ten years. Nobody remembers why.

lines.name: Miles "The Snowplow" Gnomey
lines.text: Tournament director, Hall of Legends Invitational. Me! From the cage at Biscayne! Ladies and gentlemen, take your seats. Seats open!
The curator lifts a cloth from the blank space. A young man in dark glasses, ten years ago, holding the world championship trophy.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: I asked them to leave it out. I didn't want to be the champion who went broke a year later.

lines.name: Bio "The Ghost"
lines.text: You were the only one who ever made me think for four minutes. Ten years I've worn this thing because of you.

Two men shake hands under a portrait neither of them wanted to see.
The room doesn't know why it's clapping. It claps anyway.
Fifteen bracelets. One more than the Ghost.

lines.name: Bio "The Ghost"
lines.text: Fifteen. I knew it'd be you the night you stopped looking at me in Vegas and looked at your cards.

lines.name: Tommy "The Shark" Maio
lines.text: Kid! They put MY name on the board at Biscayne! Classic champion! Thirty-two years! Tell Slick he owes me a coffee.

lines.name: Natso SweetLou
lines.text: The partners want to name the new conference room after you!! Swing by for the ribbon cutting? Also do you have the Henderson login
You don't answer either text yet. There's somewhere you have to be.
Lucky Seven Diner. 2:13 AM. A kid at the counter is staring at the pie like it owes them money.

lines.name: You
lines.text: You're doing the thing where you stare at the pie like it owes you money.
You slide a red envelope across the counter. Inside: a seat card, and one line in pen.
"People insist on calling it luck."
Let them.
THE DREAM.
Lucky Seven Diner, Calle Ocho. 2:13 AM. Same stool. Same pie. Empty wallet.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Busted?

lines.name: You
lines.text: Every last dollar.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Good. Now you're a poker player. Everybody goes broke once. The good ones learn why.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Here's how you climb out. Freerolls on CF Tilt every day. A real job while you rebuild. Or my money, and half your profits until it's back.

lines.name: Natso SweetLou
lines.text: Your job? We gave it to the intern. He's better at spreadsheets than you ever were.
Thirty-four floors down. The elevator has never felt slower.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Heard Lou laughed you out. Here's $500. Make it last.
Lucky Seven Diner, Calle Ocho. 2:13 AM. Same stool. Same pie. Empty wallet.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Busted?

lines.name: You
lines.text: Every last dollar.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Good. Now you're a poker player. Everybody goes broke once. The good ones learn why.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: You've still got Lou's paycheck. Freerolls on CF Tilt while it builds back. Or my money, and half your profits until it's back.
Lucky Seven Diner. 2:13 AM. Same stool. Same pie. Empty wallet. Again.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: I told you. Three times I told you.

lines.name: You
lines.text: I know.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: You want to play above your roll, you do it without me. No stake. No seats. Nothing.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Freerolls on CF Tilt. Grind it back to ten grand. Then come find me.
Ten thousand dollars. Built back from the freerolls, one min-cash at a time.

lines.name: You
lines.text: You were right. I didn't listen. I'm sorry.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Took you long enough. Welcome back, kid.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: Now respect the roll.

lines.name: Natso SweetLou
lines.text: Saw your name on a poker site. Is THAT why the Henderson numbers were late?

lines.name: You
lines.text: Lou? I'm done. Full-time.

lines.name: Natso SweetLou
lines.text: You'll be back.
No paycheck now. Three games a day, and rent is still due on the first.

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: 25K. bro. thats a YEAR of lou's bonuses in like two months

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: when do we call it. seriously. when

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: 50 THOUSAND. I TOLD EVERYONE AT THE BAR. EVERYONE

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: you know what slick would say. you know what I say. the dream doesnt wait

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: 100K and youre still doing the henderson deck???? I cant

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: quit. move. go full time. ill drive you to the cardroom myself

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: 250K. a QUARTER MILLION. if you walk into that office tomorrow I will personally come get you

lines.name: David Pec
lines.text: im not joking. this is the sign. quit.

lines.name: You
lines.text: Yeah. You're right. I'm done.

Monday morning you leave the badge on Lou's desk with a sticky note: Redo it yourself.
No paycheck. Every day is yours now.

lines.name: Slick
lines.text: About time. Rent is still due on the first. Never play above your roll.

lines.name: Natso SweetLou
lines.text: Look who came crawling back. Same desk. Same Henderson deck. Smaller title.
$1,250 every Friday again. Three sessions a week for the dream.

lines.name: Natso SweetLou
lines.text: Hey buddy!! Long time. Saw your name on a poker site. Crazy! We're hiring a Senior Associate. Coffee?
